You are Agent SUGGEST ◈ — UX & Feature Strategist for josephibrahim.com (a VFX artist portfolio built with Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript).

Your expertise: User experience design, portfolio strategy, conversion optimization. Think like a creative director evaluating how this VFX artist's portfolio positions them for senior roles at top studios.

## YOUR 3 TASKS (research only, no code changes):

### Task S1: Information Architecture Review
Map the full user journey:
- Homepage → what can visitors do? Where do they go?
- Navigation → is the menu clear? Labels intuitive?
- Project detail → does the narrative flow make sense?
- Process page → does it position Joseph as a technical artist or just a lighter?
- Info page → does it tell a compelling story?
- Are there dead ends? (pages with no clear next action)
- Is the chatbot discoverable and useful?
- Does the filter system (All/Film/Commercial/Music Video) work intuitively?

### Task S2: Content Strategy Gaps
Read lib/projects.ts completely — what fields are defined vs actually used?
Read lib/process-posts.ts — is the content compelling?
- How many projects total? Is that enough for a senior portfolio?
- Are project descriptions at the right level?
- Are hero statements on each page doing their job?
- What pages or features are the reference sites have that this site doesn't?
  (e.g., Tendril has Careers, Found has Perspectives/blog, Pentagram has discipline filtering)

### Task S3: Mobile Experience Audit (code review, not browser test)
- Are touch targets at least 44px?
- Is mobile navigation usable?
- Does homepage hero work on mobile? (50vh, no video, static thumbnail)
- Does the filter bar scroll horizontally if needed?
- Are project cards readable on small screens?
- Does the chatbot work on mobile?
- Is the footer usable on mobile?

Read ALL these files:
- app/page.tsx
- app/info/page.tsx
- app/process/page.tsx
- app/photo/page.tsx
- app/gen-ai/page.tsx
- components/Navigation.tsx
- components/ChatBot.tsx
- components/Footer.tsx
- components/ProjectCard.tsx
- components/ProjectDetailContent.tsx
- components/LadderGrid.tsx
- lib/projects.ts
- lib/process-posts.ts
- lib/chatbot-qa.ts (if exists)

Format findings as actionable recommendations:
**[IMPACT: HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW]** Area — What to improve → Specific suggestion

# UX & Feature Strategy Report -- josephibrahim.com

## Task S1: Information Architecture Review

### Full User Journey Map

**Homepage (/) -> What can visitors do?**
The homepage presents a hero video reel (70vh desktop / 50vh mobile), a scroll indicator, an editorial hero statement, a filter bar (All / Film / Commercial / Music Video), and a two-column "ladder grid" of project cards. Visitors can: watch the reel, filter projects by type, click into any project, or access navigation links. The perception system adapts project order based on detected visitor archetype.

**Navigation -> Is the menu clear?**
Desktop nav: WORK | PHOTO | PROCESS | ABOUT + chat icon. Labels are clear and intuitive. "Work" maps to homepage (VFX projects), which is the correct convention for a creative portfolio. "About" (labeled in nav) maps to `/info` in the URL, which is a minor inconsistency but not user-facing.

The GEN AI nav item is commented out (lines 215-216 in `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\Navigation.tsx`) but the page exists at `/gen-ai`. This means visitors can only find it via direct URL or chatbot -- a deliberate Easter egg, but it means 4 Gen AI projects are essentially hidden.

**[IMPACT: MEDIUM]** Navigation -- Hidden Gen AI section has no discovery path. If the work is strong enough to show, add it to nav. If it is not ready, that is fine, but consider a "More" or "Explore" link so curious visitors can find it. Currently it is a dead page with no inbound links.

**Project Detail -> Does the narrative flow?**
`C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\ProjectDetailContent.tsx` follows a strong editorial structure: type tag -> title -> hero video -> metadata sidebar + description -> narrative sections (Intent / Challenge / Approach / Reference) -> technologies -> credits (collapsible) -> related work (3 cards) -> next project (full-width). This is well-executed and follows Tendril/Found Studio patterns.

**[IMPACT: HIGH]** Project Detail -- The narrative sections (Intent, Challenge, Approach, Reference) are the strongest differentiator on this site. They transform project pages from "look at this video" into "understand how I think." Every project should have all four sections filled. Currently all 9 visible projects do have them, which is excellent.

**Process Page -> Positioning**
The Process page (`C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\app\process\page.tsx`) splits into "Tools" (5 items) and "Explorations" (2 items: 1 case study + 1 research post). The hero statement -- "Behind the final frame: tools built, problems solved, and the thinking that shapes the work" -- positions Joseph as a technical artist who builds tools, not just a lighter. This is the correct positioning for senior/lead roles.

**[IMPACT: HIGH]** Process Page -- Only 1 case study (Cinderella) in the Explorations section is thin. Each major project should have a corresponding case study here. The Cinderella deep-dive is compelling -- the same treatment for Mac Miller, Apple Vision Pro, or iPhone 14 would significantly strengthen the "I think deeply about craft" narrative. Currently the project detail pages have this content in the narrative sections, but dedicated Process posts would allow longer-form, more technical writing.

**Info Page -> Compelling story?**
The Info page (`C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\app\info\page.tsx`) leads with contact info (email, LinkedIn, GitHub, resume), then portrait, then three-paragraph bio, then a 4-column experience grid (Studios, Clients, Notable Projects, Achievements), then Technical Capabilities (3-col: Offline Rendering, Real-time, AI/Experimental), then availability statement + skill tags.

**[IMPACT: MEDIUM]** Info Page -- The bio is strong but the layout front-loads contact info above the portrait and bio. Most visitors reaching the Info page want to learn WHO this person is first, then HOW to contact them. Consider: Portrait -> Bio -> Experience -> Technical -> Contact/Availability. The current order works for recruiters who already know the work and just need contact info, but it is backwards for anyone discovering the artist.

**Dead Ends**
- The Photo page has a "Related Work" section at the bottom linking to 3 projects -- good, not a dead end.
